newsitem.title: UK: EBRD thrift not to blame for problems at meeting.
newsitem.headline: EBRD thrift not to blame for problems at meeting.

text.p: The head of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Tuesday he was proud of his thrifty policies but denied these were to blame for long queues and overcrowding at the bank's annual meeting.
"When you act on taxpayers' money you have to be very stringent in the way you use it," EBRD President Jacques de Larosiere told a news conference at the end of the four-day gathering in London.
He was replying to a question which linked the bank's economical approach to operational shortcomings. "I wouldn't like that to be necessarily associated with my stinginess," De Larosiere said.

The previous EBRD head Jacques Attali was criticised for lavish spending, especially on the imposing marble-floored headquarters of the bank which was set up to help former communist countries become more efficient.
De Larosiere admitted that the meeting halls in London were too small for the 5,350 people registered to attend, but he said no alternative appropriate venue was available.
Next year's annual meeting is due to take place in the Ukrainian capital Kiev.
Ukrainian officials in London expected another good attendance but said there would be no Soviet-style queues.
"You'll understand the difference when you come to Kiev in 1998," Oleg Taranov, head of the 1998 annual meeting committee, said. "But the queues for planes to Kiev might be longer."
